about: The Commerce round (Adam, Nov 19 2026): the Workfront and Commerce version pickers, four back-office systems for Adobe Commerce (ERP, PIM, order management, warehouse management), Adobe Commerce Optimizer, Adobe Commerce Intelligence and Other commerce platform, the move to Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service and multi-store setup. Read from Experience League, Adobe Help and Adobe Developer pages with a plain fetch, and from Adam's paste of the Adobe Commerce FAQ on business.adobe.com (Nov 19 2026); every quote was proven word for word on Nov 19 2026. Hours are our own estimates; Adobe publishes none.

lines.name: Assessment and plan for the move to Commerce as a Cloud Service
lines.scope: Run Adobe's Migration Assessment on your client's Commerce on Cloud or on-premises project, review its complexity rating with your client, list the custom code, extensions, data in custom tables and integrations to move, and agree the phases, the order of work and who does what between Adobe, your client and you.
lines.evidence: Every Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service migration begins with an assessment.

source.title: Experience League: Migrate to Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service

lines.name: Custom code rebuilt as App Builder apps for Cloud Service
lines.scope: Rebuild each of your client's Commerce customizations and extensions that has no Cloud Service equivalent as an App Builder app using Commerce APIs, events and webhooks, start from the Commerce Developer Agent where it helps, review all generated code before production, and test each app against the agreed behavior.
lines.evidence: Modernizing a store's customizations for this architecture is typically the most significant engineering effort in an Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service migration.

source.title: Experience League: Migrate to Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service

lines.name: Data migration to Commerce as a Cloud Service
lines.scope: Set up your client's store settings and system configuration on the new instance first, move products, customers and orders with Adobe's bulk data migration tool, which Adobe provides through its Commerce Deployed Engineering engagement, build an App Builder job for data held in custom tables by third-party extensions, and reconcile record counts.
lines.evidence: Configuration settings (store settings, system configuration) are not migrated automatically and must be set up on the target instance independently prior to migration.

source.title: Experience League: Bulk data migration tool

lines.name: Integrations and storefront rebuilt for Cloud Service
lines.scope: Re-establish each of your client's back-office integrations on the new instance through APIs, events and App Builder, point the storefront at it and test every data flow end to end. The storefront build itself on Edge Delivery Services is the service Build the Commerce storefront on Edge.
lines.evidence: Customizations are modernized into App Builder applications, storefronts are rebuilt on Edge Delivery Services (EDS), data is migrated into the new Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service tenant, and integrations are re-established using SaaS patterns.

source.title: Experience League: Migrate to Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service

lines.name: Cutover to Commerce as a Cloud Service
lines.scope: Plan and rehearse the cutover with your client, run the final data sync, switch traffic to Commerce as a Cloud Service, check orders, payments and search on the live store, retire the old platform and hand over to ongoing operation.
lines.evidence: Cut over and operate - Switch traffic to Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service, decommission legacy systems, and transition into ongoing operation.

source.title: Experience League: Migrate to Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service

lines.name: Multi-store, multi-brand and multi-region setup
lines.scope: For each brand, store or region beyond the first, add its website, store and store views on the same Admin, a store view for each language, its allowed currencies and rates, its tax rules, the inventory sources and stock that serve it, and its local payment and shipping options, then test an order in each.
lines.evidence: Within each website, you can have multiple stores, and within each store, separate store views.

source.title: Experience League: Store and site structure

lines.name: Search and merchandising configuration on Cloud Service
lines.scope: On Commerce as a Cloud Service, where Adobe installs and connects the search and catalog services, set your client's catalog views and policies, search facets, synonyms and merchandising rules, then test search, category browse and filters on the storefront.
lines.evidence: Configure catalog views and policies to define storefront product assortments. Apply merchandising rules across all catalog views or tailor them to a specific view. Configure product recommendations, search facets, and synonyms.

source.title: Experience League: Merchandising Services powered by catalog views and policies

lines.name: B2B setup on Cloud Service
lines.scope: On Commerce as a Cloud Service, where the core B2B features come installed, turn on company accounts, shared catalogs, quotes and purchase orders for your client, create the first company accounts with credit limits and custom pricing, and test company roles, quotes and approvals.
lines.evidence: Full B2B capabilities available after installation Pre-installed with core B2B features

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Commerce feature comparison

lines.name: Monthly on-premises hosting operations
lines.scope: Each month, run your client's on-premises Commerce servers: capacity planning and scaling, backups and disaster recovery tests, monitoring and alerts, and security patches for the operating system, PHP, database and middleware.
lines.evidence: Capacity planning, auto scaling, clustering, backups, disaster recovery

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Commerce on-premises installation overview

lines.name: Commerce Optimizer instance and user setup
lines.scope: Set up your client's sandbox and production Commerce Optimizer instances, match each to the commerce and storefront environments of the same kind, add users in the Adobe Admin Console with the roles each team needs, and record the instance IDs and endpoints.
lines.evidence: Connect sandbox Optimizer instances to non-production commerce and storefront environments. Connect production Optimizer instances to production commerce and storefront environments.

source.title: Experience League: Get started with Adobe Commerce Optimizer

lines.name: Catalog views, policies and price books in Commerce Optimizer
lines.scope: Design your client's catalog views for each brand, market, language or sales channel, the policies that filter what each view shows, and the price books each view uses, then check each view returns the agreed products and prices.
lines.evidence: Within Adobe Commerce Optimizer, you can manage your catalog by creating catalog views and policies that best define your business goals.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Commerce Optimizer overview

lines.name: Search, recommendations and merchandising in Commerce Optimizer
lines.scope: Set your client's search facets, synonyms and merchandising rules, add the product recommendations agreed for each page type, check storefront events arrive, and train the merchandisers to run them.
lines.evidence: In addition, the merchandiser can provide personalized experiences to drive traffic and engagement using product discovery, recommendations​, and intelligent merchandising.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Commerce Optimizer overview

lines.name: Data warehouse tables and calculated columns in Commerce Intelligence
lines.scope: Choose the tables and columns your client's reports need, set them to sync in the Data Warehouse Manager, and build the calculated columns for the agreed measures, such as customer lifetime value and repeat orders.
lines.evidence: Using the Data Warehouse Manager, you can manage table and column sync settings, drill down into a table's schema, and create calculated columns to use in reports.

source.title: Experience League: Data Warehouse Manager

lines.name: Commerce Intelligence dashboards and reports
lines.scope: Build the dashboards and reports your client's teams agreed, such as sales, customers, products and acquisition sources, check each number against Commerce, and walk the teams through reading and filtering them.
lines.evidence: Adobe Commerce Intelligence Dashboards give you a quick view of your store's performance and sales activity at a glance.

source.title: Experience League: Commerce Intelligence dashboards

lines.name: Scheduled report emails and exports from Commerce Intelligence
lines.scope: Set up the scheduled emails your client's teams want from Commerce Intelligence dashboards, and show them how to export chart data to a CSV or Excel file.
lines.evidence: learn how to export and share data from a chart to a .csv or Excel file.

source.title: Experience League: Share data from a chart

lines.name: Other data into Commerce Intelligence by file or API
lines.scope: Bring in the other data your client's reports need: upload agreed CSV files on a schedule, or write scripts that send data through the Adobe API, then join it to the Commerce tables in the data warehouse.
lines.evidence: There are four ways to get your data into Commerce Intelligence: connect a database, connect a SaaS integration, upload a .csv file, or use the Adobe API.

source.title: Experience League: Connecting data (Commerce Intelligence)

connections.how: The partner builds this on Adobe's Commerce integration starter kit, which runs in Adobe Developer App Builder, or installs a prebuilt connector from Adobe Exchange where one fits the ERP. Commerce sends order, customer and product events through Adobe I/O Events to App Builder actions that call the ERP's APIs, and the ERP's stock, price and order status changes come back to Commerce through its APIs. Webhooks let Commerce ask the ERP for an answer at once, such as taxes or order totals, before it goes on.

source.title: Adobe Developer: Install Adobe Commerce integration starter kit

gain.title: Orders and stock shared with the ERP
gain.text: Orders placed in Commerce reach your client's ERP without re-entry, and the ERP's stock, prices and order status reach Commerce.

flows.what: Order, customer and product events, transformed and sent to the ERP's APIs

source.title: Adobe Developer: Expose Commerce data

flows.what: Stock, product, price and order status updates, written to Commerce through its APIs

source.title: Adobe Developer: Enrich the shopping experience

lines.name: Commerce to ERP integration
lines.scope: Build the integration between Adobe Commerce and your client's ERP on Adobe's Commerce integration starter kit in App Builder: map order, customer, product and stock fields, deploy the actions for each, subscribe to the Commerce events, connect the actions to the ERP's APIs, set retries and test. Where a prebuilt connector on Adobe Exchange fits the ERP, install and configure it instead.
lines.evidence: Integrating Adobe Commerce with your enterprise resource planning (ERP), order management system (OMS), or customer relationship management (CRM) is now easier with Adobe Commerce integration starter kit.

source.title: Adobe Developer: Install Adobe Commerce integration starter kit

lines.ext: an ERP with APIs the integration can call

lines.name: Live ERP answers at checkout with webhooks
lines.scope: Set up Commerce webhooks that call your client's ERP when Commerce needs an answer at once, such as order totals, taxes or payments, write the answer back into Commerce, set timeouts and what happens when the ERP does not answer, and test them under load.
lines.evidence: Synchronous calls are required when Commerce needs to compute or validate something immediately (order totals, taxes, payments) using a 3rd-party endpoint and write the result back into Adobe Commerce.

source.title: Adobe Developer: Adobe Commerce Webhooks overview

lines.name: Admin screens to run the back-office sync
lines.scope: Add pages to your client's Commerce Admin with the Admin UI SDK where the team sets up the back-office sync, sees what was sent and what failed, and sends a record again.
lines.evidence: Integrate third-party systems - Connect to ERP, CRM, or warehouse management systems for data sync and operations management.

more_evidence.quote: The Migration Assessment is only available when migrating Adobe Commerce on Cloud Infrastructure or Adobe Commerce on-premises projects to Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service.
Implementation decisions and architecture validation remain collaborative activities between Adobe, partners, and customer engineering teams.
Data held in custom tables by third-party extensions is identified during assessment, but it is not handled by the standard data migration and requires an App Builder customization.
The Commerce Developer Agent allows you to migrate existing application, extension, and module code to App Builder, or to create new development from scratch.
You must review all generated code before using it in a production environment.
The bulk data migration tool is a Docker-based CLI that system integrators run on their own migration machine.
Many installations have one website and one store, but with multiple store views to support different languages.
Allowed Currencies — Select all currencies that you accept as payment in the store view.
Tax calculations are managed at the website level.
You can use Inventory Management for a single source or a multi-source network that includes warehouses, stores, pickup locations, drop shippers, and other fulfillment locations.

Adobe Commerce empowers businesses to support multiple storefronts for various brands, product lines, or geographic regions, all from a single platform and managed through a single administrative interface.
Multiple inventory locations can be configured to maintain accurate stock levels across regions, and prebuilt extensions make it easy to integrate with local payment and shipping options.
To enable access to Adobe Commerce Optimizer, add users from the Adobe Admin Console and ensure that they have access to the Commerce product.
Adobe Commerce Intelligence Dashboards give you a quick view of your store's performance and sales activity at a glance.
Access to the bulk data migration tool is provided exclusively through a Commerce Deployed Engineering (CDE) engagement.
